title: Move the Cables to Connect All Computers

concept.title: Each move can join two groups, and a spare cable is any cable that closes a cycle
body: A network has `n` computers and `m` cables, each cable joining two computers. In one move you can take a cable (it stays attached to nothing meanwhile) and plug it between **any** two computers. What is the fewest moves needed so that every computer can reach every other one?

Think in components. If the network falls into `c` groups, you must join them, and joining two groups needs one cable, so you need at least `c - 1` moves. Are there enough cables? A connected network of `n` computers needs `n - 1` cables at least. If `m < n - 1`, there are not enough cables at all: print -1. If `m >= n - 1`, there are always enough **spare** cables (cables that sit on a cycle inside a group and can be removed without splitting the group), so exactly `c - 1` moves are enough.

Counting the components is the task you already know (a search or union-find). The reasoning, "a lower bound plus a construction that reaches it", is the typical way to solve this kind of problem without simulating the moves.

statement: A network has `n` computers (numbered 1 to n) and `m` cables; a cable joins two computers. In one move you can take any cable and plug it between any two computers instead. Print the smallest number of moves after which every computer can reach every other one, or -1 if it is impossible.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `m`: the number of nodes (numbered 1 to n) and the number of edges.
Each of the next `m` lines has two numbers `u` and `v`: an edge between the nodes `u` and `v`.
outputFormat: Print the number of moves or -1.
constraints: There are no self-loops and no repeated edges.

examples.note: There are two groups, {1, 2, 3} and {4, 5, 6}. The cable 2-3 is spare; move it to join the groups: 1.
Five cables are needed to connect six computers, but there are only 3: -1.

hints: Connecting c components needs c - 1 cables, and the whole network needs at least n - 1 cables.
If m < n - 1 print -1, otherwise print c - 1.

input = sys.stdin.readline

n, m = map(int, input().split())
edges = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]

explanation: Connecting the network needs at least n - 1 cables; if there are fewer the answer is -1. Otherwise there are enough spare cables, and exactly (number of components - 1) moves are needed.
solution.complexity: Time O(n + m), space O(n + m).
